Vegetation Kit

Reference Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: assets/vegetation-kit/manifest.json

A nine-asset CC0 kit for exercising PBR, alpha cutout and blend foliage, shadows, GI and LOD, plus the demo scene that wires it together.

The Vegetation Kit is a small, self-contained set of nine CC0 assets for exercising the renderer: PBR materials, alpha-cutout and alpha-blended foliage, shadow casting, Photon GI, baked AO, instancing and automatic LOD.

The kit lives in assets/vegetation-kit/ in the engine repository. Every model is 1k PBR and every material ships the albedo, normal and ARM (AO / roughness / metallic) maps used by the engine.

Contents#

Asset Role Triangles Alpha Caffeine material
fir_sapling Tree 433,021 Opaque fir_sapling_branches.mat, fir_sapling_twigs.mat
tree_stump_01 Stump / bark 41,046 Opaque tree_stump_01.mat
shrub_03 Bush 8,287 Cutout shrub_03.mat
shrub_sorrel_01 Ground shrub 3,319 Cutout shrub_sorrel_01.mat
fern_02 Fern 6,232 Cutout fern_02.mat
grass_medium_02 Grass 7,842 Blend grass_medium_02.mat, _cutout.mat
celandine_01 Flowers 8,966 Blend celandine_01.mat, _cutout.mat
nettle_plant Tall plant 31,304 Cutout nettle_plant.mat
moss_01 Ground cover 204 Cutout moss_01.mat, _blend.mat

A total of 540,221 triangles across nine assets, 41.8 MB including textures. All assets are CC0 1.0 from Poly Haven. The individual source URLs and authors are in manifest.json; a human-readable list is in ATTRIBUTION.txt.

previews/ contains the Poly Haven thumbnails used by this page and by asset browsers.

Quick start#

Copy the kit into the project's assets directory:

bash
cp -r assets/vegetation-kit <project>/assets/

The paths in the .gltf and .mat files are project-relative (assets/vegetation-kit/...), so the kit must keep that layout inside the project.

Demo scene#

scenes/vegetation-kit.caf contains a ground plane, a camera, a directional sun, a warm point light, a Photon GI component and 29 vegetation meshes. The point light is there to exercise point shadows and local GI, and the camera uses the same 16:9 framing as the screenshot above.

  • Doppio: copy the kit into the project, then open assets/vegetation-kit/scenes/vegetation-kit.caf.
  • Runtime: set the project's start scene:
json
{
  "last_scene": "assets/vegetation-kit/scenes/vegetation-kit.caf"
}

then run caffeine-runtime --project <project>.

The scene is intentionally lit with a lower exposure (PostProcessComponent exposure 0.9) than a default project. If you reuse the assets in a brighter scene, tune the exposure rather than the material colours.

Use one asset#

  1. Drag a model into the viewport, for example assets/vegetation-kit/models/fern_02/fern_02.gltf.
  2. Select the entity and open Inspector → Mesh Filter.
  3. Set Custom Material to the matching .mat, for example assets/vegetation-kit/materials/fern_02.mat.
  4. Enable Cast Shadows and Receive Shadows as needed.

The full PBR path is the .mat file. The glTF also contains a usable base colour material, so it renders without a .mat; assigning the .mat adds the normal map, ARM map, alpha mode and alpha cutoff.

What each asset tests#

Feature Assets What to look for
Opaque PBR tree_stump_01, fir_sapling Bark grain, normal detail and AO from the ARM map
Alpha cutout fern_02, shrub_03, shrub_sorrel_01, nettle_plant Hard leaf edges, stable shadows, no sorting
Alpha blend grass_medium_02, celandine_01, moss_01 blend variants Soft edges and sorted transparent surfaces
Shadows All assets + demo scene Tree and stump cast onto the ground; the warm point light casts local shadows
Photon GI Demo scene environment View → Photon Global Illumination; try Debug → GI only
Baked AO tree_stump_01, fern_02, shrub_03 Bake from the Photon panel and inspect the new ORM map
Instancing grass_medium_02, fern_02, celandine_01 Duplicate entities and compare draw cost
Automatic LOD fir_sapling 433k-triangle source; the renderer builds medium/far clustered LODs
Multi-material fir_sapling Split into branches + twigs so each part can use a full PBR material

fir_sapling is the heaviest asset in the kit and is the best stress test for the LOD path. For a lighter tree, scale the split branches/twigs down or use the stump as an opaque PBR control.

Alpha modes#

The glTF importer now reads alphaMode (OPAQUE, MASK, BLEND) and alphaCutoff into MeshSurfaceMaterial, and the renderer applies the mode per submesh. This means a tree can have an opaque trunk and a cutout leaf submesh in the same mesh.

For this kit:

  • Cutout is the default for ferns, shrubs and the grass/moss cutout variants. It writes depth and is the cheapest path for foliage shadows.
  • Blend is the default for grass and celandine and is available as moss_01_blend.mat. It gives softer edges but requires sorting and does not write depth.
  • The albedo PNGs contain alpha. Poly Haven publishes the diffuse and alpha maps separately; the kit composites them into a single RGBA albedo so the same texture works in the engine and in external glTF viewers.

If leaf edges shimmer, raise alpha_cutoff slightly (for example 0.45 → 0.55) or use the blend variant. Very thin geometry may need doubleSided; the kit's glTF materials are double-sided, and the engine currently disables back-face culling globally.

Tree parts#

fir_sapling uses two materials (branches and twigs), and Caffeine custom materials apply to a whole mesh. The kit therefore ships two single-material glTFs:

  • models/fir_sapling/fir_sapling_branches.gltf → fir_sapling_branches.mat
  • models/fir_sapling/fir_sapling_twigs.gltf → fir_sapling_twigs.mat

Add both entities at the same position and scale. The demo scene already does this. The complete fir_sapling.gltf is also present for viewers or pipelines that support multi-material meshes directly.

Baked AO and GI#

The demo scene has a PhotonGIComponent on the Environment entity. Use the native Photon panel to switch presets or inspect the GI-only view.

To bake static AO:

  1. Select a custom mesh such as Tree Stump or Fern.
  2. Open View → Photon Global Illumination.
  3. In Baked ambient occlusion, choose resolution/rays and press Bake selected mesh.

The baker writes an ORM PNG under the project's processed assets and updates the assigned .mat. Bake on a copy of the kit if you want to keep the original material files unchanged. Primitive meshes (the demo ground) are not suitable bake targets; use the stump or a kit plant.

Feature checklist#

  • [x] PBR albedo, normal and ARM maps
  • [x] Alpha cutout and alpha blend variants
  • [x] Shadow casting and reception
  • [x] Photon GI component in the demo scene
  • [x] Baked AO targets with unique UVs
  • [x] Instancing-friendly repeated meshes
  • [x] High-poly source for automatic LOD
  • [x] Multi-material tree split into single-material parts

Licensing#

All assets are CC0 1.0 Universal (public domain). Attribution is not required, but the original authors are listed in ATTRIBUTION.txt and the manifest for provenance:

  • Poly Haven: https://polyhaven.com
  • CC0 1.0: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/

The license text is in LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt.

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Fix
Model is white or untextured Assign the matching .mat; the glTF alone only carries base colour
Textures are missing Keep the whole assets/vegetation-kit/ tree; the .gltf and .mat files use relative texture paths
Scene looks washed out Lower PostProcessComponent.colorGrading.exposure or the light intensities; the demo uses 0.9
Tree appears as two pieces Add both fir_sapling_branches.gltf and fir_sapling_twigs.gltf at the same transform
Leaf edges are hard Increase alpha_cutoff or switch to the _blend variant
Ground tiling is too visible Edit uv_tiling in materials/ground.mat (demo uses 20×20)
Plant shows a yellow skeleton The Skeleton component is present. Remove it, or keep it only if you explicitly used Fit humanoid rig. New imports no longer get a rig automatically.
LOD pops Expected; tune the renderer's LOD distance scale or use the lower-poly plants
